evidence_note: Supplies the Maya track's first sourced judgment layer: the four year-bearer prognostics of Landa, quoted from a public-domain edition with its Spanish original, together with the rules that keep them conditional, communal and colonially framed. It also records, as a rule, that Landa carries no per-day-sign birth augury, so that the absence is a documented finding rather than an assumption.

conclusion.source_quotation_es: Dexando con las cerimonias hechas, echado el demonio, segun su engaño, este año tenian por bueno, porque reynava con la letra Kan el Bacab-Hobnil, del qual dezian no avia peccado como sus hermanos y por esso no les venian miserias en el.
conclusion.engine_rendering: Once the ceremonies were done and the demon cast out - so their delusion ran - they held this year for a good one, because with the letter Kan there reigned the Bacab Hobnil, of whom they said that he had not sinned as his brothers had, and that for this reason no miseries came upon them in it.
conclusion.qualification: The witness immediately qualifies the verdict: because miseries nevertheless often occurred, services were prescribed so that when they did occur the blame could be laid on the services or their performers.

conclusion.source_quotation_es: Este año en que la letra Muluc era dominical y el Bacab Canziemal reynava, tenian por buen año, ca dezian que era este el mejor y mayor destos dioses Bacabes; y ansi le ponian en sus oraciones el primero.
conclusion.engine_rendering: This year, in which the letter Muluc was dominical and the Bacab Canzicnal reigned, they held for a good year, for they said that this was the best and greatest of these Bacab gods, and so they put him first in their prayers.
conclusion.qualification: The same passage nevertheless names the year's miseries - little water, and maize throwing many shoots - and prescribes the idol Yax-Coc-Ahmut and its offerings as the remedy. The witness adds that they had many other miseries and bad signs, although the year was good, if they did not perform the prescribed services.

conclusion.source_quotation_es: Tenian tambien un pronostico de que alguños de los que quisiessen ser señores no prevalescerian. Dezian ternian tambien langosta, y que se despoblarian muchos de sus pueblos de hambre.
conclusion.engine_rendering: They also had a prognostic that some of those who wished to be lords would not prevail. They said they would likewise have locusts, and that many of their towns would be depopulated by hunger.
conclusion.qualification: The section is headed in the edition 'Sacrificios del año nuevo de la letra Yx. Pronosticos malos y modo de remediar sus efectos'. The facing French column expands the same prognostic: a year bad for bread but abundant in cotton, a great lack of water, days of excessive sun that would dry the maize fields, famine, and from famine thefts, and from thefts slavery, and hence discord and civil war, and changes among the lords or the priests.

conclusion.source_quotation_es: Este año en que la letra era Cauac y reynava el Bacab-Hozanek tenian, allende de la pronosticada mortandad, por ruyn, por que dezian les avian los muchos soles de matar los maizales, y comer las muchas hormigas lo que sembrassen y los paxaros, y porque esto no seria en todas partes avria en algunos comida, la qual avrian con gran trabajo.
conclusion.engine_rendering: This year, in which the letter was Cauac and the Bacab Hozanek reigned, they held - besides the mortality it was threatened with - for a wretched one, because they said the many suns would kill the maize fields, and the many ants and the birds would eat what they sowed; and because this would not be so everywhere, in some places there would be food, which they would have only with great labour.
conclusion.qualification: The remedy prescribed is four idols named Chichac-Chob, Ek-Balam-Chac, Ahcan-Uolcab and Ahbuluc-Balam, with the fire ceremony described in the same section.

conclusion.requirement: the prescribed remedy stated in the same section must be reported with the verdict
conclusion.reason: in this witness no prognostic stands alone; each is paired with a prescribed observance, and the text explicitly says that when miseries came anyway the blame was laid on the observance
conclusion.consequence: a verdict quoted without its remedy converts a conditional ritual system into a fatalistic one, which the source does not support

exceptions: Never present a Landa year verdict as an unconditional outcome.
